questions.question:
Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

14 × 16 ÷ 8 + 2 – 1 = 17
questions.solution:
Given equation:- 14 × 16 ÷ 8 + 2 – 1 = 17

We need to be interchanged two signs for making the correct equation , so we check the option,

1) 14 + 16 ÷ 8 × 2 – 1 = 17

14 + 2 × 2 – 1 = 17

14 + 4 – 1 = 17

18 – 1 = 17

17 = 17

Thus, the correct answer is “ + and × ”.

questions.question: In a ceratin code language, ROGER’ is written as ‘5’ and ‘MOULDS’ is written as ‘6’. What will be the code for ‘PIN’ in that code language?

MOULDS → Total Digit of word is 6.

Similarly,

**PIN → Total Digit of word is 3.**

Thus, the correct answer is 3.

K is three places above P. If we arrange these chairs in alphabetical order from top to bottom, then the position of how many chairs (excluding J) will be remains same?

questions.question:
If + is interchanged with -, then what will be the value of the following equation?

72 – 91 ÷ 13 × 12 + 6 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation is:- 72 – 91 ÷ 13 × 12 + 6 = ?

If + is interchanged with – then,

72 + 91 ÷ 13 × 12 - 6 = ?

72 + 7 × 12 - 6 = ?

72 + 84 - 6 = ?

156 - 6 = ?

150.

Thus, the correct answer is “150”.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) form the statements.

Statements:

I. Some bikes are cars.

II. Some cars are trucks.

Conclusions:

I. Some trucks are bikes.

II. No bike is a truck.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c30214ada7e7d3819e6f6f0848fad3d2c7c77ac5a0b672c48d0ae56e9e7e6c1.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some trucks are bikes** → **False (No direct relation given)

II. No bike is a truck** → **False (No direct relation given)

Conclusion I and II makes complementary pair for either.

Thus, Either conclusion I or II follows.

questions.question:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

72, 69, 64, ?, 48
questions.solution:
The pattern used here is:-

72 – 3 = 69,

69 – 5 = 64,

**64 – 7 = 57,**

57 – 9 = 48.

Thus, the correct answer is “57”.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements in true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

I. All T are M.

II. No T is P.

Conclusions:

I. No P is M.

II. Some M are T.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34a03b1381e7f459ffcfb6fcbc34335d1f1b2c45d94f0df1ae73a555d7e93298.png] 

**__Conclusion__:**

I. No P is M** → False** (There is no direct relation given between P and M so it can be possible but not definite, hence, false)

II. Some M are T** →** **True** (as "All T are M" given so some M are T it is definite, hence, true)

Thus, **"Only conclusion II follows"** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
